meta.name: Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102)
meta.notes: 10 questions across the major AI-102 domains (planning, generative AI, agentic, computer vision, NLP, knowledge mining & document intelligence). Distractors hardened with realistic near-miss services and answer positions rebalanced. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass

questions.question: You are deploying Azure AI capabilities for an enterprise app and need a single endpoint and key that authorise calls to Vision, Language, Speech and Translator with consolidated billing. Which resource type should you create?
options: One single-service resource created separately for each API you call
An Azure API Management gateway placed in front of four single-service resources
A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposing one shared key
An Azure AI Foundry hub workspace used on its own as the inference endpoint
questions.explanation: A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposes a single endpoint and key that authorise Vision, Language, Speech, Translator and other Azure AI APIs, and rolls all usage onto one bill. Creating one single-service resource per API leaves you managing a separate endpoint and key for every service. An API Management gateway can unify routing in front of those resources, but you still provision, pay for and manage each one — it adds a layer rather than consolidating the service. An Azure AI Foundry hub organises projects, models and connections; it is not the resource that serves the inference APIs.

questions.question: Your team must rotate the access keys on a production Azure AI Language resource without interrupting client traffic that is already in flight. Which sequence is recommended?
options: Regenerate the currently unused key, move all clients to it, then rotate the other

Regenerate both key1 and key2 at the same time, then redeploy every client app simultaneously — regenerating both keys simultaneously causes a window where all clients using the old keys receive authentication errors during the rotate
Regenerate the key that clients are actively using and let them reconnect to it
Abandon key authentication entirely and switch the resource over to Entra ID tokens
questions.explanation: Azure AI resources expose two keys precisely so you can rotate with zero downtime: regenerate the key no client is currently using, migrate every client to that freshly rotated key, then regenerate the other. Regenerating both keys at once invalidates every live connection until all clients are redeployed. Regenerating the key clients are actively using breaks their in-flight calls immediately. Switching to Microsoft Entra ID tokens is a valid authentication model, but it replaces key authentication rather than rotating the keys the question asks about.

questions.question: A retailer wants to detect and locate their own product SKUs inside shelf photographs using a small set of labelled images and a no-code training portal. Which Azure service fits best?
options: Azure AI Vision Image Analysis 4.0, relying only on its built-in object tagging without labelled images — the built-in model recognises generic objects but cannot be trained on custom labelled images to detect domain-specific items like safety equipment or branded products
Azure AI Document Intelligence with a custom-trained field-extraction model
Azure AI Video Indexer using a custom-trained brand-and-object model
An Azure AI Custom Vision object-detection project trained on labelled images
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision lets you upload a small set of labelled images in a no-code portal and train an object-detection model that returns bounding boxes for your own product SKUs. Image Analysis 4.0 recognises only generic objects from Microsoft's prebuilt taxonomy and cannot learn specific SKUs. Document Intelligence extracts fields from forms and documents, not products on a shelf. Video Indexer analyses video timelines and needs video input — it is not a still-image SKU detector even with its custom brand support.

questions.question: The prebuilt invoice model in Azure AI Document Intelligence is missing several vendor-specific fields that your finance team needs extracted automatically. What should you do next?
options: Switch the prebuilt invoice model over to its receipt-extraction variant — the prebuilt receipt model extracts standard receipt fields such as merchant and total; it does not support vendor-specific custom fields that require a trained model built from labelled documents
Label a few vendor-specific documents and train a custom extraction model
Run the Read OCR model and parse the missing fields with regular expressions
Compose the prebuilt invoice model together with the prebuilt receipt model
questions.explanation: When a prebuilt model omits fields you need, you label a small set of representative documents in Document Intelligence Studio and train a custom extraction model that learns those vendor-specific fields. The prebuilt invoice model has no 'receipt variant' to switch to — invoice and receipt are separate prebuilt models with different schemas. Running Read OCR and regex parsing discards the layout and key-value structure the service already understands, making extraction brittle. Model composition combines several custom models behind one endpoint for routing; it does not add new fields to a prebuilt model.

questions.question: Your chatbot must classify each user utterance into an intent and extract entities such as dates and locations from it. Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
options: Custom named entity recognition (custom NER) configured on its own — custom NER extracts named entities from text but does not interpret the intent or extract slot values from conversational language understanding utterances
Sentiment analysis with opinion mining enabled on each utterance
Conversational language understanding (CLU) with a trained model
An orchestration workflow that routes utterances to other projects
questions.explanation: Conversational language understanding (CLU), the successor to LUIS, is purpose-built to predict an intent and extract entities from each utterance within a single trained model. Custom NER extracts entities only and has no concept of intents. Sentiment analysis with opinion mining returns sentiment polarity and aspect-level opinions, not intents. An orchestration workflow connects and routes between CLU, custom question answering and other projects — it relies on an underlying CLU project to do the intent-and-entity work rather than doing it itself.

questions.question: A studio wants Azure to speak marketing copy in a voice that reproduces a specific brand spokesperson, built from professional studio recordings of that person. Which capability is required?
options: Custom Neural Voice trained on the spokesperson's studio recordings

A prebuilt neural voice chosen from the standard text-to-speech catalogue — standard neural voices are pre-built and generalised; they do not match the brand spokesperson's specific voice characteristics or studio recordings
Personal Voice, the instant zero-shot voice-cloning capability
An SSML voice style-and-role applied to a standard neural voice
questions.explanation: Azure Custom Neural Voice (the Professional tier) trains a synthetic voice from professional studio recordings of a real, consented speaker so it reproduces that spokesperson's identity, and is gated by Microsoft's Limited Access programme to prevent misuse. A prebuilt catalogue voice is a generic Microsoft speaker and cannot match a named person. Personal Voice also clones a voice, but it is the zero-shot, consumer-oriented option built from a very short sample — not the studio-trained brand voice described here. SSML voice styles and roles only adjust the expression of an existing voice; they cannot create a new speaker's identity.

questions.question: You want an Azure OpenAI chat deployment to answer questions using your own private PDF policy documents, kept up to date with each release. Which pattern is recommended?
options: Fine-tune the GPT model on the PDF text to embed the Azure documentation into the model weights — fine-tuning bakes knowledge into the model weights at training time; it does not keep the indexed PDFs up-to-date in Azure AI Search when documentation changes
Paste the entire text of every policy PDF into the system prompt on each call
Raise the deployment's context window and stream all PDFs in with each request
Index the PDFs in Azure AI Search and query them via the On Your Data feature
questions.explanation: The recommended Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern is to chunk and embed the PDFs into an Azure AI Search index, then point the Azure OpenAI 'On Your Data' feature at that index so each query retrieves only the relevant passages. Fine-tuning teaches style and format rather than fresh facts, and re-running it every release is slow and costly. Pasting every PDF into the system prompt — or simply enlarging the context window to fit them all — burns tokens, raises latency and cost, and still loses accuracy as the document set grows. Only indexed retrieval scales and stays current as policies change.

questions.question: By default, every Azure OpenAI deployment screens prompts and completions for harmful content across categories such as hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content. Which capability provides those built-in filters?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud AI workload threat-protection rules — Defender for Cloud monitors deployment-level security posture and threat signals; it does not apply inline content filters to block specific categories in the model deployment response stream
Azure AI Content Safety filters integrated into the deployment
Azure Policy initiatives scoped to generative AI resources
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels applied to the model output
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI deployments include Azure AI Content Safety filters by default; they score every prompt and completion for hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content against severity thresholds, and also provide Prompt Shields and protected-material detection. Microsoft Defender for Cloud, including its AI threat-protection plan, watches for attacks and posture problems against the resource — it does not classify message content. Azure Policy enforces how resources are configured, not what text users send. Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels classify and protect data for governance and DLP; they do not moderate harmful content in model traffic.

questions.question: Your assistant must call live external APIs (weather, inventory) during a chat turn and weave the results back into its reply. Which Azure OpenAI capability orchestrates that pattern?
options: Fine-tune the model on transcripts of previous real API responses
Embed the entire API reference documentation into every system prompt
Function (tool) calling, with a tools schema supplied in the request
Switch the deployment to the Assistants API code-interpreter tool
questions.explanation: Function (tool) calling lets the model emit a structured JSON call matching a tools schema you define; your application runs the real weather or inventory API and returns the result, which the model then weaves into its reply. Fine-tuning on past transcripts bakes in stale snapshots and never calls a live API. Embedding API reference docs in the prompt only describes the APIs — it cannot invoke them and wastes tokens. The Assistants API code-interpreter tool runs sandboxed Python for data analysis, not arbitrary external API calls, so it does not orchestrate this pattern.

questions.question: You add a 1,536-dimension embedding produced by Azure OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 to each chunk in an Azure AI Search index so it can be retrieved by vector similarity. How should that field be defined?
options: Collection(Edm.Single) with a dimensions value and a vector profile
Collection(Edm.Double) marked searchable with the standard text analyzer — a Double field does not support vector search operations and cannot accept a dimensions property
Edm.String set as both searchable and filterable for similarity queries
A complex field wrapping 1,536 numeric sub-fields, one per dimension
questions.explanation: A vector field in Azure AI Search is typed as Collection(Edm.Single) — a single-precision float array — and must declare a `dimensions` value (1536 here) plus a vector search profile that selects an algorithm such as HNSW. Collection(Edm.Double) is not a valid vector element type, and a text analyzer is meaningless for numeric vectors. Edm.String holds keyword text for full-text search and cannot back vector similarity. A complex type groups named sub-fields for structured objects and cannot be queried as a single embedding vector.
